output.title: Spot duplicate emails before they become cleanup work
output.body:
If you run a small business and duplicate emails keep showing up, the real question is not “can AI fix this?” It is: do the duplicates reach you before you act on them?

That is the bounded workflow decision. If the answer is yes, the cost is usually not technical complexity; it is wasted review time, inconsistent replies, or manual cleanup later. That is enough reason to look at the process, but not enough reason to automate blindly.

Start with three recent examples. For each one, write down where the duplicate came from: a system syncing the same contact twice, the same person sending again, or you copying a thread into another tool. Then mark which duplicates must be caught before action and which can be cleaned up later. An invoice or payment request belongs in the first group; a newsletter usually does not. Human approval stays in place for anything involving money or other high-risk decisions.

One practical next step: run a one-week manual test. Route suspicious duplicates to one folder and review them by hand. Count the repeats, the false positives, and the time your own review takes. If the pattern is messy, that is useful too. It means the next step is a clearer definition of “duplicate,” not a bigger tool. Sometimes the boring answer is the useful one.
